# Ed’s Tokenized Securities Rails
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/index


A human-curated, LLM-maintained, source-linked knowledge base on **tokenized securities infrastructure**: issuers, legal structures, custody, chains, venues, settlement and regulation. Every fact links to a source; unverified fields say `unknown`.

## New to tokenization?
Here is the life of a token in four steps, and how a real (native) share differs from a wrapper. Read the full [[overview|overview]].

<a href="/overview" style="display:block;background:none;padding:0"><picture>
<source media="(max-width: 700px)" srcset="/diagrams/overview-mobile.svg">
<img src="/diagrams/overview-desktop.svg" alt="How tokenized securities work in four steps: issue, approve buyers, trade and settle, pay holders; plus native vs wrapper. See the overview page for a text version" style="width:100%;height:auto">
</picture></a>

*[See the detailed version](/overview#the-full-picture)*

## Why tokenize securities?
Today, buying a stock or bond goes through a chain of brokers, [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodians]] and [[concepts/glossary#ccp|clearinghouses]]. Each one keeps its own records and has to reconcile them with the others, which is why settlement takes days and markets close at night. A token puts the asset and its ownership record on one shared ledger, so:

- **Cash and asset swap in one step.** Both sides settle together or not at all ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp260826~3641116314.en.html)).
- **Markets don't need to close.** Trades could clear in seconds, 24/7 ([BlackRock](https://www.blackrock.com/corporate/investor-relations/2025-larry-fink-annual-chairmans-letter)).
- **Assets plug into other things.** Tokenized Treasuries can already be posted as collateral for futures and swaps ([CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9146-25)).
- **More people get access.** You can own fractions, from anywhere.

It's already real for big institutions, though two common numbers measure different things. About \$368B of repo trades *settle every day* on Broadridge's blockchain platform: that is a daily flow, with the same cash and bonds lent and repaid over and over ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2025/broadridge-distributed-ledger-repo-platform-november)).

Tokenized Treasuries *held* on blockchains total about \$14.5B as of Oct 2026: that is a stock of assets, like an account balance ([rwa.xyz](https://app.rwa.xyz/treasuries)). Most tokenized assets so far are bonds and [[concepts/glossary#money-market-fund|money market funds]] ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

Many stock tokens are wrappers: a third party holds the real share and gives you a token that tracks it, usually without a vote ([[overview#native-vs-wrapped|native vs wrapper]]).

# Tokenized securities: how it fits together
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/overview
type: overview

<picture>
<source media="(max-width: 700px)" srcset="/diagrams/overview-mobile.svg">
<img src="/diagrams/overview-desktop.svg" alt="How tokenized securities work in four steps: issue, approve buyers, trade and settle, pay holders; plus native token versus wrapper" style="width:100%;height:auto">
</picture>

*[See the detailed version](#the-full-picture)*

## Why tokenize securities?
Today, buying a stock or bond goes through a chain of brokers, [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodians]] and [[concepts/glossary#ccp|clearinghouses]]. Each one keeps its own records and has to reconcile them with the others, which is why settlement takes days and markets close at night. A token puts the asset and its ownership record on one shared ledger, so:

- **Cash and asset swap in one step.** Both sides settle together or not at all ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp260826~3641116314.en.html)).
- **Markets don't need to close.** Trades could clear in seconds, 24/7 ([BlackRock](https://www.blackrock.com/corporate/investor-relations/2025-larry-fink-annual-chairmans-letter)).
- **Assets plug into other things.** Tokenized Treasuries can already be posted as collateral for futures and swaps ([CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9146-25)).
- **More people get access.** You can own fractions, from anywhere.

It's already real for big institutions, though two common numbers measure different things. About \$368B of repo trades *settle every day* on Broadridge's blockchain platform: that is a daily flow, with the same cash and bonds lent and repaid over and over ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2025/broadridge-distributed-ledger-repo-platform-november)).

Tokenized Treasuries *held* on blockchains total about \$14.5B as of Oct 2026: that is a stock of assets, like an account balance ([rwa.xyz](https://app.rwa.xyz/treasuries)). Most tokenized assets so far are bonds and [[concepts/glossary#money-market-fund|money market funds]] ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

Many stock tokens are wrappers: a third party holds the real share and gives you a token that tracks it, usually without a vote ([[overview#native-vs-wrapped|native vs wrapper]]).

*For readers who know capital markets (and maybe crypto at a high level) but not how the pieces connect. This page covers what is new compared with traditional rails; the linked pages go deeper.*

## How to use this wiki
- **New to this?** Read the "Why" above, then the diagram at the top, then [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]].
- **Stuck on a word?** Look it up in the [[concepts/glossary|glossary]].
- **Comparing platforms?** Use the [database](/database) of issuers and venues.
- **Using an AI assistant?** Start with the [starter prompts](/starter-prompts) or the [guide for agents](/agents).
- **Following rule changes?** Check the [changelog](/changelog/) or [subscribe](/subscribe) for updates.

## The one-sentence version
A tokenized security is an ordinary stock or bond whose ownership record lives on a shared digital ledger, so trading, settling and paying dividends can run automatically.

## What's actually different from today's rails
- **One shared record instead of many copies.** Today the official list of who owns a share sits with a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] or central depository, and every bank and broker in between keeps its own copy that has to be checked against the others. With tokens, everyone works from the same ledger, and the token balance can be the official record. The BIS says this joins "messaging, reconciliation and asset transfer into a single, seamless operation" ([BIS AER 2025, ch. III](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)). A transfer agent often stays involved for regulatory reasons ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).
- **Cash and asset swap at the same moment.** If the payment is also a token on the same ledger, one transaction can move the security one way and the cash the other: both happen or neither does. This is called [[concepts/glossary#atomic-settlement|atomic]] [[concepts/glossary#dvp|delivery versus payment]] (DvP) ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)). The digital cash can be central bank money, tokenized bank deposits or [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoins]] ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)), and which one is used changes the risk ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)). More: [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]].
- **The rules travel with the token.** Securities law still applies, so the token itself can refuse a transfer to a [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallet]] that has not passed identity checks, and the issuer can freeze or recover tokens. ERC-3643 is one standard that works this way ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)). See [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]], [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400]], [[standards/solana-token-2022|Token-2022]].
- **Always open, and reusable.** The ledger never closes, and the same token can be plugged into other uses such as collateral or lending ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). The flip side is that tightly linked systems can pass problems along; WEF flags the risk of "limitless composability" ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)).

## Native vs wrapped
There are two ways to put a share on a ledger, and which one you hold decides what you actually own.
- **Native: the token is the share.** The company, or its transfer agent, issues the security on the ledger, and your token balance is the official ownership record ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf); [SEC staff, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)). Examples: [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]], [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] transfer-agent issuances.
- **Wrapper: a claim on a share.** The real share stays with a custodian or broker in the traditional system, and a third party issues a token that tracks it. SEC staff split wrappers into custodial ones (a claim on the held share) and [[concepts/glossary#synthetic-wrapper|synthetic]] ones (a separate contract, such as a note or swap) ([SEC staff](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)). Someone has to keep the number of tokens matched to the shares held, and you can only swap back through the issuer ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)).

> **Downsides of holding a wrapper.**
> - You own a claim on a firm that holds the share, not the share itself.
> - Usually no voting rights ([SEC staff](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).
> - You rely on that firm to keep the share safe and to [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] it ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)). If it fails, you can lose money even if the company behind the share is fine: Robinhood warns its EU stock-token buyers they could lose up to their full investment if Robinhood becomes insolvent ([Robinhood EU](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)).
> - The token can trade at a different price from the share.
> - The company behind the share may not have agreed: 22 companies had objected to tokens of their shares on OKXICE by 23 Oct 2026 ([[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv#issuer-objections|OKXICE objections]]).

The legal wrapper decides what the holder actually owns. More: [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy]], [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] and [[comparisons/implementations-by-model|implementations by model]].

## The full picture
The same four steps in detail: who does what at each step, the traditional role each part replaces, and how native and wrapped tokens differ.

<picture>
<source media="(max-width: 700px)" srcset="/diagrams/overview-detailed-mobile.svg">
<img src="/diagrams/overview-detailed-desktop.svg" alt="Detailed diagram of how tokenized securities work. 1 Issue: the issuer and transfer agent create a security token on a shared 24/7 ledger. 2 Approve buyers: an identity allowlist means only KYC'd wallets can hold it. 3 Trade + settle: 3a Match on a trading venue (order book, RFQ or onchain pool); 3b Check the wallet allowlist and pre-funded legs; 3c Settle by atomic DvP, swapping the security token for a cash token in one transaction; 3d Record balances and update the register. 4 Pay holders: dividends, votes and redemptions go to investor wallets. A side panel contrasts native tokens (the token is the register) with wrapped tokens (a 1:1 claim on a share held by a custodian)." style="width:100%;height:auto">
</picture>

## The four steps in the diagram
1. **Issue.** The issuer, or its transfer agent, creates tokens and keeps them in sync with the official register. For wrappers, a custodian holds the underlying shares.
2. **Approve buyers.** Investors are checked once ([[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]]) and their wallets are added to an [[concepts/glossary#allowlist|allowlist]], and every transfer checks the list. This replaces part of what opening an account does today. See [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]].
3. **Trade + settle.** This is where tokenized rails differ most from today's, so it is broken into four parts below.
4. **Pay holders.** Dividends, splits, votes and redemptions run through the token contract or the issuer's agent. See [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|Corporate actions & dividends]] and [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]].

## Inside step 3: trade and settle
- **3a Match.** Orders still meet on a familiar venue, such as an exchange or [[concepts/glossary#ats|ATS]] order book or a broker's [[concepts/glossary#rfq|RFQ]], or in an [[concepts/glossary#amm|onchain pool]] or AMM, as in [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|permissioned pools]] and the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|onchain-venue (TSV) model]]. Matching can happen off-chain with only settlement on the ledger, or entirely on-chain. Several US models keep the traditional book and tokenize post-trade only: see the [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|post-trade / Reg NMS model]] and the [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTC tokenization pilot]].
- **3b Check (pre-trade).** The token contract checks that the receiving wallet is eligible ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)). Because on-ledger settlement is usually trade by trade (gross), both legs typically have to be in place up front. Projects that "eliminate principal counterparty risk" do so by requiring "high levels of liquidity, often through [[concepts/glossary#prefunding|prefunding]] on a platform" ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)), rather than the [[concepts/glossary#netting|netting]] and credit that today's CCPs and brokers provide.
- **3c Settle.** A [[concepts/glossary#smart-contract|smart contract]] swaps the security token for the cash token in one transaction, so both legs settle or neither does ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)). IOSCO describes a range of settlement models. At one end the ledger is only shared books and records, and [[concepts/glossary#settlement-finality|settlement finality]] "remain[s] with the [[concepts/glossary#csd|CSD]]". At the other is DLT-native settlement, with assets and settlement instruments on the same ledger or linked ones ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). Finality is still a legal question, not just a technical one: final settlement "is a legally defined moment" ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)).
- **3d Record (post-trade).** Wallet balances update at once. For [[concepts/glossary#native-token|native tokens]] that is the register update. For wrapped tokens, or where a transfer agent keeps the official register, the books must still be updated or reconciled against the ledger ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/); [IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). Regulatory reporting still applies.

**Trade-offs.**
- **Pre-funding.** It removes settlement exposure but costs liquidity. The FSB warns that higher prefunding needs at scale could weaken resilience to liquidity shocks ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)). IOSCO notes that CCP functions such as netting could in time be encoded in smart contracts ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).
- **Market hours.** An always-on ledger does not make 24/7 trading automatic. WEF calls always-on infrastructure "a design choice dependent on market demand, risk tolerance and technology" ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)).
- **Cash leg.** The choice of cash token matters. The CPMI-IOSCO principles favour central bank money where practical and available, as cited by [WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/).

## Mapping to familiar roles
| TradFi role | Tokenized equivalent |
|---|---|
| Registrar / transfer agent / CSD | Token contract (native) or custodian plus token (wrapped); transfer agent often remains ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)) |
| Account opening / KYC | Identity registry and allowlist ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)) |
| Exchange / ATS / broker | Same roles, or an onchain venue |
| CCP netting + T+1 settlement via CSD | Pre-funded, trade-by-trade atomic DvP on the ledger ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)) |
| Cash in bank or central bank accounts | Tokenized deposits, wholesale CBDC or stablecoins ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)) |
| Brokerage account | Custodial or self-held wallet ([[topics/custody|Custody]]) |

## Formal definitions
CPMI: "the process of generating and recording a digital representation of traditional assets on a programmable platform" ([CPMI 2024](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d225.htm)). IOSCO: the "creation, issuance, or representation of assets on a digital token ledger or a programmable platform" ([IOSCO 2025](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

## Where it stands
Adoption is real but early. IOSCO finds it "incipient and incremental," led by fixed income and money market funds (see the [[comparisons/buidl-precedent|BUIDL precedent]]). A lack of cross-chain interoperability and of credible settlement assets limits scale, and many participants still use traditional trading and post-trade infrastructure ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

The FSB sees no material stability risk at today's small scale. It names liquidity and maturity mismatch, leverage, asset quality, interconnectedness and operational fragility as the vulnerabilities to watch ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)). The BIS argues for a "unified ledger" with tokenised central bank reserves, commercial bank money and government bonds at its centre ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)).

Regulators broadly apply "same activities, same risks, same regulatory outcomes" ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). For the US and EU specifics, see [[topics/regulation|Regulation]] and [[concepts/international|International]].

## Text version of the diagram
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S1[1 Issue: company or agent creates tokens on a shared ledger] --> S2[2 Approve buyers: only KYC-checked wallets can hold]
  S2 --> S3[3 Trade + settle: 3a match, 3b check wallet, 3c token and cash swap at once, 3d record]
  S3 --> S4[4 Pay holders: dividends, votes, redemptions]
  N[Native: the token is the share] -.- S1
  W[Wrapper: a third party holds the share; the token is a claim on it] -.- S1
```

# Guide for AI agents
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/agents


Ed’s Tokenized Securities Rails is a human-curated, LLM-maintained, source-linked knowledge base on tokenized securities infrastructure. This page is for AI agents reading the live site. Working from a clone of the repo? Read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/edyavno/edstokenizedsecuritiesrails/blob/main/AGENTS.md) instead.

## Fast ways in
- [`https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms.txt`](https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms.txt): one line per page with a short summary.
- [`https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms-full.txt`](https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms-full.txt): every page in one plain-text file.
- [[starter-prompts|Starter prompts]]: example questions this wiki can answer.

## URL patterns
| URL | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/<page>` | Companies that issue tokenized securities or stock tokens |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/platforms-venues/<page>` | Exchanges, trading venues and exchange rule filings |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/infrastructure/<page>` | Settlement, oracle, DeFi and tokenization infrastructure |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/<page>` | Token standards (ERC-3643, ERC-1400, Token-2022, B20) |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/<page>` | Legal and market-structure concepts |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/<page>` | Cross-cutting explainers (custody, settlement, regulation, ...) |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/<page>` | Side-by-side comparisons of models and precedents |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/changelog/<page>` | Dated change entries |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/overview` | How the pieces fit together, with a diagram |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/database` | One table of all issuers, venues and infrastructure |

Folder URLs (e.g. `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/`) list their pages. Entity pages open with an **At a glance** box (type, jurisdiction, chain, status, last updated) and end with **Sources**. `unknown` means not yet verified from a public source.

## Freshness
Pages appear about 30 days after facts are recorded. Check each page's *last updated* date and confirm time-sensitive facts against the linked source.

## How to cite
Cite the page URL and its last-updated date, e.g. "Ed’s Tokenized Securities Rails, *Dinari dShares*, https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/dinari (last updated 2026-10-17)". For a specific fact, prefer the original source linked on the page.

# Starter prompts
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/starter-prompts


Example questions an AI agent can answer from this wiki alone. Point the agent at `/llms-full.txt` (or clone the site repo) and ask:

## Structures and rights
- Which issuers offer native shares on the issuer's register, and which offer wrapped or derivative tokens? Cite the page for each.
- Compare bStocks, xStocks and Robinhood Stock Tokens by legal structure, jurisdiction and who can buy.
- What rights does a holder of a Dinari dShare have compared with a Superstate Opening Bell holder?

## Venues and settlement
- How does Nasdaq's approved tokenized securities rule keep tokenized and traditional shares on the same order book?
- What does the DTC no-action letter allow, and which venue rules reference the DTC pilot?
- Summarize the OKXICE TSV design under the Innovation Exemption: access, pairs and custody.

## Standards and infrastructure
- Compare ERC-3643, ERC-1400 and Solana Token-2022 on how they enforce transfer restrictions.
- How do Chainlink tokenized equity feeds handle stock splits and multipliers?
- How do Uniswap v4 permissioned pools enforce issuer allowlists?

## Regulation and markets
- Which entities are US-regulated versus offered only outside the US? Build a table with jurisdiction and status.
- What does the SEC staff statement on tokenized securities say about issuer-sponsored versus third-party tokens?
- How are dividends and corporate actions handled across issuers? Note any that are `unknown`.

## Tips
- Ask the agent to cite page URLs and `last_updated` dates, and to say `unknown` rather than guess.
- Data is published with a 30-day delay; check the linked sources for anything time-sensitive.

========================================================================

# Glossary
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/glossary
type: concept

*In plain English: short definitions of the terms this wiki uses, A to Z. Each one links to a source and to the pages that go deeper.*

New to all of this? Start with the [[overview|overview]], then come back here when a word trips you up. Reference information only, not investment advice.

Jump to: [A](#a) · [B](#b) · [C](#c) · [D](#d) · [E](#e) · [I](#i) · [K](#k) · [L](#l) · [M](#m) · [N](#n) · [O](#o) · [P](#p) · [R](#r) · [S](#s) · [T](#t) · [W](#w)

## A

### Allowlist
A list of approved wallet addresses. A permissioned token only moves to wallets on the list, which is how identity checks are enforced onchain. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643 (T-REX)]] · [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]]

### AMM
An automated market maker: a smart contract holding a pool of two assets that prices trades by formula instead of matching buyers and sellers. Also called an onchain pool or liquidity pool. ([BIS CPMI](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d225.htm))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap v4 permissioned pools]] · [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model]]

### Atomic settlement
Both sides of a trade settle in one indivisible step: either everything moves or nothing does. Atomic DvP is the common case. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### ATS
An alternative trading system: an SEC-regulated venue run by a broker-dealer that matches orders but is not a full stock exchange. ([Figure](https://investors.figure.com/news-releases/news-release-details/figure-announces-chain-public-equity-network-open-running))

*Related:* [[issuers/figure-open|Figure OPEN]]

### Authorized Participant
A large firm, usually a market maker, allowed to create (mint) and redeem tokens directly with the issuer. Ordinary holders buy and sell on the market instead. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]] · [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase Tokenized Stocks]]

## B

### B20
The token standard on Base that Coinbase's tokenized stocks use. ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]]

### Bankruptcy-remote
Set up so that if the parent company fails, its creditors cannot reach the assets held for token holders. ([Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/tokenize))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

### Base
A layer 2 blockchain built on Ethereum and run by Coinbase. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]] · [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase Tokenized Stocks]]

### Broker-dealer
A firm registered with the SEC to buy and sell securities for customers (broker) or for itself (dealer). Most people buy stocks through one. ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

## C

### CCP
A central counterparty, or clearinghouse. It steps between buyer and seller so each side faces it instead of each other, and nets trades to reduce how much cash and stock must move. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Composability
Tokens on the same chain can plug into other apps, for example being posted as loan collateral, without special integration work. ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### CSD
A central securities depository: the institution that holds securities centrally and records who owns them at the top level. In the US that is DTC. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]

### CUSIP
The 9-character ID code for a US security, like a serial number for a stock or bond. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model]]

### Custodial wrapper
A token backed one-for-one by a real share held at a custodian. You own a claim on that share, not the share itself. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

### Custodian
A regulated firm that holds assets for someone else. For wrapped tokens, the custodian holds the real shares behind the tokens. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

## D

### DLT
Distributed ledger technology: a shared database copied across many computers. Blockchains are one type. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### DTC
The Depository Trust Company, the US central securities depository. It runs a tokenization pilot under an SEC no-action letter. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]

### DTCC
The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation, parent of DTC. It provides clearing and settlement for most US stock trades. ([DTCC](https://communications.dtcc.com/rs/669-QIL-921/images/DTCC%20Tokenization%20Service%20At-a-Glance.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]

### DvP
Delivery versus payment: the security is delivered only if the payment is made. Onchain, both legs can move in one transaction (atomic DvP). ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

## E

### ERC-1400
A draft Ethereum standard suite for security tokens, with transfer checks, documents and forced transfers. ([Spec](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400 / ERC-1410]]

### ERC-20
The basic Ethereum token standard. Most tokens, including many stock tokens, follow it or extend it. ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview))

*Related:* [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]]

### ERC-3643
An Ethereum standard for permissioned tokens: a transfer only goes through if both wallets pass identity and compliance checks. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643 (T-REX)]]

### ETF
An exchange-traded fund: a fund whose shares trade on an exchange like a stock. ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/backeds-xstocks-go-live-today-on-bybit-kraken-and-solana-defi-302494374.html))

*Related:* [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks (Backed)]]

### Ethereum
A public blockchain that runs smart contracts. Many token standards (ERC-20, ERC-3643) were written for it. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]]

### Exemptive relief
Permission from the SEC to do something an existing rule would otherwise forbid, usually with conditions. ([WisdomTree](https://ir.wisdomtree.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/777/wisdomtree-to-launch-247-trading-and-instant-settlement))

*Related:* [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree tokenized funds]] · [[topics/regulation|Regulation]]

## I

### Innovation Exemption
A temporary, conditional SEC order from 17 Sep 2026 that lets approved onchain venues (TSVs) trade tokenized US stocks. ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model]]

## K

### KYC
Know your customer: identity checks a firm must run before letting you open an account or hold certain assets. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]]

## L

### Layer 2
A blockchain that runs on top of another (usually Ethereum) to make transactions cheaper and faster. Base is one. Also written L2. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]]

## M

### Mint
To create new tokens. For backed stock tokens, tokens are minted when the matching shares are bought and put in custody. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]]

### Money market fund
A fund that invests in very short-term, low-risk debt such as Treasury bills. Many of the largest tokenized products are money market funds. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree tokenized funds]] · [[comparisons/buidl-precedent|BUIDL (adjacent fund precedent)]]

### Multiplier
A number that converts one token into shares of the underlying stock. It changes after splits or reinvested dividends so token balances stay the same while each token is worth more or fewer shares. Also called rebasing. ([xStocks docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers))

*Related:* [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|Corporate actions & dividends]]

## N

### Native token
A token that is the security itself: the token balance is the official register of who owns it. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### Netting
Adding up all of a firm's trades and settling only the difference. It cuts how much cash and stock must move, but needs a central party and time. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### NMS stock
A stock listed on a US national exchange and covered by Reg NMS, the rules that tie US stock markets together. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model]]

### No-action letter
A letter from SEC staff saying they will not recommend enforcement if a firm does a specific thing under stated conditions. It is not a rule change. ([SEC DTC no-action letter](https://www.sec.gov/files/tm/no-action/dtc-nal-121125.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]] · [[topics/regulation|Regulation]]

## O

### Oracle
A service that feeds outside data, such as a stock price, into a blockchain so smart contracts can use it. ([Chainlink](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/tokenized-equity-feeds))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/chainlink-equity-feeds|Chainlink tokenized equity feeds]]

## P

### Prefunding
Putting the full cash and the full securities in place before a trade, because atomic settlement leaves no time to borrow or net. It costs liquidity. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

## R

### Redeem
To hand tokens back to the issuer in exchange for the underlying asset or its cash value. Usually limited to eligible holders or Authorized Participants. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

### Reg NMS
Regulation National Market System: SEC rules that link US stock exchanges, including best-price and order-protection rules. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model]]

### Repo
A repurchase agreement: a short-term loan where one side sells bonds and agrees to buy them back later at a slightly higher price. ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2025/broadridge-distributed-ledger-repo-platform-november))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### RFQ
Request for quote: you ask one or more dealers for a price and trade at the quote you accept, instead of using a public order book. ([Robinhood](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Rule 15c3-3
The SEC customer protection rule. It requires broker-dealers to keep customers' securities in their possession or control and separate from the firm's own. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

### RWA
Real-world asset: a traditional asset such as a bond, fund or stock represented as a token. ([rwa.xyz](https://app.rwa.xyz/treasuries))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

## S

### Settlement finality
The point at which a transfer can no longer be reversed and ownership has legally changed. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Smart contract
A program stored on a blockchain that runs automatically when its conditions are met, for example a swap that only completes if both sides pay. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]]

### Solana
A public blockchain known for fast, low-cost transactions. Its Token-2022 program supports compliance features. ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions))

*Related:* [[standards/solana-token-2022|Solana Token-2022 extensions]]

### SPV
A special purpose vehicle: a company set up only to hold certain assets or issue certain securities, kept separate from its parent. ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory))

*Related:* [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] · [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo Global Markets (Ondo Stocks)]]

### Stablecoin
A token designed to keep a steady value, usually one US dollar, backed by cash and short-term government debt. ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Synthetic wrapper
A token that is a separate security, such as a note or swap, that tracks a stock's price. It may not be backed one-for-one by real shares. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

## T

### T+1
Trade date plus one business day: the current US settlement cycle for most stock trades. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Token-2022
Solana's newer token program, with add-ons such as transfer hooks and frozen-by-default accounts that support permissioned tokens. ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions))

*Related:* [[standards/solana-token-2022|Solana Token-2022 extensions]]

### Tokenized deposit
A bank deposit represented as a token. It is a claim on a regulated bank, unlike a stablecoin. ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Transfer agent
The firm a company appoints to keep its official register of shareholders and record transfers. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]] · [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]]

### Transfer hook
Code that runs automatically on every token transfer, for example to check the receiving wallet is allowed. ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook))

*Related:* [[standards/solana-token-2022|Solana Token-2022 extensions]]

### TSV
Tokenized Securities Venue: an onchain venue approved under the SEC's Innovation Exemption to trade tokenized US stocks. ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model]] · [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]

## W

### Wallet
Software or hardware that holds the keys controlling tokens. A custodial wallet is run by a firm; a self-custody wallet is run by you.

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

### Wrapper
A token that represents a share held by someone else, rather than being the share itself. See custodial wrapper and synthetic wrapper. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

# Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/innovation-exemption
type: concept

*In plain English: The SEC now lets a few approved onchain venues trade tokens of US stocks, for a limited time and under conditions. This page explains how that works and who objects.*

On 17 Sep 2026 the SEC issued an order (Rel. 34-106402, File 4-927) granting temporary, conditional section 36(a)(1) relief ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf); [press release](https://business.cch.com/srd/SECgov_SECIssuesInnovationExemptiontoFacilitatetheTradingofTokenizedNMSStockandRequestforComment091726.pdf)):
- **Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs)** operating permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm|AMM]] liquidity pools are exempt from the definition of "exchange".
- **Covered Firm** liquidity providers are exempt from the definition of "dealer".
- **Conditions** include U.S. person and OFAC compliance, a 30-day public notice, issuer notice and objection for third-party tokens, same rights as the underlying, public auditable [[concepts/glossary#smart-contract|smart contracts]] on a permissionless ledger, and synchronized halts ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf)).
- **Caps**: Tier 1 cannot exceed 75 symbols and 0.25 percent of prior-month average daily share volume; Tier 2 cannot exceed 250 symbols and 2.5 percent ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf); [Skadden](https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/09/sec-innovation-exemption-establishes)).
- Synthetics are excluded; the order expires five years after publication ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf)).

Chairman Atkins framed it as a bridge to durable rulemaking ([statement](https://business.cch.com/srd/SECgov_StatementontheInnovationExemption_ABridgeTowardDurableRulemaking091726.pdf)). Law-firm analyses: [Skadden](https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/09/sec-innovation-exemption-establishes), [Davis Polk](https://www.davispolk.com/insights/client-update/sec-s-innovation-exemption-opens-path-tokenized-stock-trading), [WilmerHale](https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/client-alerts/20261005-the-innovation-exemption-arrives-sec-clears-a-conditional-path-for-onchain-trading-of-tokenized-nms-stocks).

## Issuer objection
For third-party tokens, the issuer gets notice and can object during the 30-day window ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf)). Explainer applied to the first notice: [Dida Labs](https://didalabs.com/tokenized-stock-objection/) (analysis). First test: by 21 Oct 2026, 16 issuers, including Goldman Sachs, Microsoft, Alphabet and McDonald's, had objected to OKXICE listings ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tokenized-stocks-us-companies-object.html), news).

The contrast CNBC draws: offshore volume is mostly perps and [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]] tokens that never needed issuer permission, while the US path gives issuers a say ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tokenized-stocks-us-companies-object.html)). See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv]].

## Stablecoin legs
TSV pools pair against payment [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoins]]; the GENIUS Act (S.1582, P.L. 119-27) defines permitted payment stablecoins and 1:1 reserves ([GENIUS Act](https://www.congress.gov/119/bills/s1582/BILLS-119s1582enr.htm)).

First notice: [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]. Primitive: [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap permissioned pools]].

## Sources

- <https://business.cch.com/srd/SECgov_SECIssuesInnovationExemptiontoFacilitatetheTradingofTokenizedNMSStockandRequestforComment091726.pdf>
- <https://business.cch.com/srd/SECgov_StatementontheInnovationExemption_ABridgeTowardDurableRulemaking091726.pdf>

# International regimes
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/international
type: concept

*In plain English: How rules for tokenized securities differ outside the US, region by region.*

**EU [[concepts/glossary#dlt|DLT]] Pilot Regime**: ESMA's 2025 review found low uptake, with only [[concepts/glossary#csd|CSD]] Prague, 21X and 360X authorised; barriers include thresholds, interoperability, central-bank money and legal uncertainty. ESMA recommends making the regime permanent and wider ([ESMA report](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-06/ESMA75-117376770-460_Report_on_the_functioning_and_review_of_the_DLTR_-_Art.14.pdf); [ESMA press](https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/esma-suggests-amendments-dlt-pilot-regime-make-it-permanent)).
**Offshore issuer domiciles** in this wiki: Jersey (xStocks, Robinhood), BVI (Ondo), ADGM (bStocks, Coinbase). See [[topics/regulation|regulation]].
Not yet collected: MiCA/MiFID II detail, UK Digital Securities Sandbox, Swiss DLT Act, Singapore, Hong Kong.

- <https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/esma-suggests-amendments-dlt-pilot-regime-make-it-permanent>

# Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/legal-taxonomy
type: concept

*In plain English: The SEC sorts tokenized stocks into a few legal types. This page explains each one, because the type decides what you actually own.*

The SEC staff statement of 28 Jan 2026 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)) is the vocabulary used throughout this wiki:
- **Issuer-sponsored tokenization**: the issuer (or its agent) integrates [[concepts/glossary#dlt|DLT]] into its securityholder records; the onchain record is, or feeds, the master securityholder file. Examples: [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]], [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] transfer-agent issuances.
- **Third-party tokenization**, split into:
  - **Custodial / security entitlement**: a third party holds the security and the token evidences an entitlement (e.g. UCC Article 8). Examples: Securitize Stocks, Coinbase [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]], [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] Tokenized Entitlements ([[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|post-trade model]]).
  - **Synthetic / linked**: the token is a separate security (e.g. a note) or security-based swap referencing the stock. Examples: Ondo Stocks (notes), Robinhood Stock Tokens (debt securities), bStocks (certificates).
- Format does not change legal obligations ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities); analysis: [Sidley](https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2026/01/sec-staff-unveils-a-playbook-for-tokenized-securities), [Jones Day](https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2026/02/sec-staff-provides-its-views-on-taxonomies-associated-with-tokenized-securities)).

## Broker-dealer custody
[[concepts/glossary#rule-15c3-3|Rule 15c3-3]] possession-and-control applies to crypto asset securities. The 2020 special-purpose [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]] statement is not mandatory ([SEC TM FAQ](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-relating-crypto-asset-activities-distributed-ledger-technology)). The 17 Dec 2025 TM statement describes how a broker-dealer establishes physical possession. It covers:
- the ability to transfer the asset
- private-key protections
- network risk assessment
- contingency plans

Sources: [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers); [Sidley](https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2025/12/sec-issues-further-crypto-asset-security-guidance-addresses-broker-dealer-physical-possession).

See also [[comparisons/implementations-by-model|implementations compared by model]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2026/01/sec-staff-unveils-a-playbook-for-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2026/02/sec-staff-provides-its-views-on-taxonomies-associated-with-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-relating-crypto-asset-activities-distributed-ledger-technology>
- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers>
- <https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2025/12/sec-issues-further-crypto-asset-security-guidance-addresses-broker-dealer-physical-possession>

# Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model
type: concept

*In plain English: In this model a tokenized share is the same share as the normal one. It trades on the same exchanges and only the record-keeping behind it changes.*

In this model the security does not change: tokenized and traditional shares share one order book, priority, CUSIP, symbol and rights, and settle through [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]]'s tokenization pilot ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)). Components:
- **DTC Tokenized Entitlements** under the 11 Dec 2025 [[concepts/glossary#no-action-letter|no-action letter]] ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]]).
- **Exchange rules**: [[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]] (approved 18 Mar 2026), [[platforms-venues/nyse-ice-tokenized-platform|NYSE]].
Contrast with the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|onchain-venue model]] ([[concepts/glossary#tsv|TSVs]]).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/tm/no-action/dtc-nal-121125.pdf>
- <https://www.nyse.com/publicdocs/nyse/markets/nyse/rule-filings/sec-approvals/2026/%28SR-NYSE-2026-17%29_34-105260.pdf>

# Token primitives
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/token-primitives
type: concept

*In plain English: The basic technical building blocks that tokenized stocks are made of, and which projects use which.*

The building blocks used by tokenized-stock implementations:
- **Identity-gated transfers**: [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]] (identity registry + compliance), [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400]] (transfer validation, partitions), [[standards/solana-token-2022|Token-2022 transfer hooks]].
- **Plain ERC-20** with offchain eligibility: Robinhood Stock Tokens are standard ERC-20s ([Robinhood](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/)); Ondo uses ERC-20 on Ethereum/BNB Chain ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).
- **[[concepts/glossary#multiplier|Multipliers]] for corporate actions**: build transactions in raw amounts, display raw x multiplier (xStocks, [docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers)); [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]] scaled UI amount; see [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]].
- **Permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm|AMMs]]**: [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap v4 permissioned pools]].
- **[[concepts/glossary#oracle|Oracles]]** for a 24/5 underlying traded 24/7: [[infrastructure/chainlink-equity-feeds|Chainlink]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview>
- <https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers>

# Corporate actions & dividends
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends


*In plain English: How dividends, stock splits and votes reach you depends on how the token is built. This page compares the approaches.*

How a dividend or split reaches a token holder depends on the model (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Multiplier (rebasing) model
[[concepts/glossary#wrapper|Wrapped]] tokens usually reinvest dividends and raise a multiplier rather than pay cash.
- **xStocks**: dividends are reinvested net of withholding; splits and reverse splits scale the multiplier ([xStocks docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/dividends-and-stock-splits)). Kraken computes the change as the net dividend (after 30% US withholding) divided by the prior close, and updates it around 8 p.m. EST the day before the ex-date ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)). Holders get no voting rights.
- **Coinbase on Base ([[standards/b20|B20]])**: cash dividends are converted to shares and reflected in the multiplier (e.g. 1.02 means one token [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeems]] for 1.02 shares). Scheduled updates give advance onchain notice via ERC-8056 ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- Robinhood also uses multipliers that reflect reinvested dividends ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary).

## Issuer-sponsored and fund tokens
The token is the share, so corporate actions follow the register (Superstate). Exodus's tokens carry no economic rights of their own; those attach to the Class A share ([Exodus offering circular](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm)). WisdomTree's WTGXX accrues income daily and pays monthly in cash or [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]], or reinvests it ([WisdomTree FAQ](https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/)).

## DTC
At launch, [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pays Treasury distributions in fiat to participants' traditional accounts. Equity and [[concepts/glossary#etf|ETF]] corporate actions on tokens are on the 2027+ roadmap ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/>
- <https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks>
- <https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/dividends-and-stock-splits>
- <https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>
- <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm>
- <https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/>

# Custody
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/custody


*In plain English: Who holds the real share, and who controls the token, differs by model. This page shows who keeps what.*

Who holds the real share, and who holds the keys, differs by model (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Backed (third-party) models
Backed models hold the underlying shares with a [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] or broker-dealer (Ondo: US broker-dealers; Dinari: registered US broker-dealer; Coinbase: bankruptcy-remote structure) ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary; [Fensory](https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms), secondary). SEC staff note that holders of third-party tokens may face risks, such as the third party's bankruptcy, that holders of the underlying share would not ([SEC staff statement, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).

## Issuer-sponsored models
These replace custody with a transfer-agent register: the token is the ownership record (see [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]], [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]]).

## DTC tokenized entitlements
Tokens are backed 1:1 by securities held at [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]], and DTC keeps the official books and records ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC Tokenization Service]]; [DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)).

## Broker-dealer custody of tokens
SEC staff will not object to a broker-dealer treating itself as having "physical possession" of a crypto asset security under Rule 15c3-3(b)(1) if conditions are met, chiefly control of the private keys and safeguards against their theft or loss ([SEC staff statement, 17 Dec 2025](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers)). This is a staff statement, not a rule.

## Vendors
[[infrastructure/zerohash|Zerohash]] markets a tokenization engine to brokerages ([Zerohash](https://zerohash.com/industries/brokerages)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/>
- <https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms>
- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers>
- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>

# Legal structures
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/legal-structures


*In plain English: Tokenized stocks come in a few legal forms. Some are the real share; others are a claim or a note that tracks it.*

Tokenized stocks fall into distinct legal models ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/)):
- **Debt security / certificate** backed by shares (Robinhood, bStocks, xStocks).
- **Beneficial claim** on custodied shares (Coinbase [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]]).
- **Issuer-sponsored shares** recorded by a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] (Securitize, Superstate Opening Bell).
- **Blockchain-native equity** (Figure FGRS).
- **Same security, tokenized form** inside the US market structure (Nasdaq / [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pilot, [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)).
Rights differ: backing does not automatically confer shareholder rights.

========================================================================
# Regulation
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/regulation


*In plain English: The main US and international rule changes for tokenized securities, in date order.*

Key US milestones: [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] [[concepts/glossary#no-action-letter|no-action letter]] (11 Dec 2025) and SEC approval of Nasdaq's tokenized trading rule (18 Mar 2026) ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)); WisdomTree's [[concepts/glossary#exemptive-relief|exemptive relief]] for 24/7 fund-share trading (Feb 2026, [WisdomTree](https://ir.wisdomtree.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/777/wisdomtree-to-launch-247-trading-and-instant-settlement)). Non-US issuers sit in Jersey, BVI and ADGM ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/)).

# Settlement & matching
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/settlement-and-matching


*In plain English: How tokenized stock trades get matched and settled, and how that differs from today's next-day settlement.*

Tokenized stocks trade and settle in several ways (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Venue models
- **Centralized exchanges** list tokens: Kraken trades most xStocks 24/5, with 10 trading 24/7 on Kraken Pro; withdrawn tokens can trade 24/7 on DEXs ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)).
- **Onchain DEXs**: [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]] tokens trade permissionlessly in DeFi pools.
- **Tokenized Securities Venues** run permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm|AMM]] pools under the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]]. Conditions include symbol and volume caps, a 30-day issuer objection window, and trading halts in step with the primary market ([SEC order 34-106402](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)). See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]] and [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap permissioned pools]].
- **[[concepts/glossary#ats|ATS]]**: Figure's blockchain stock settles on Provenance in YLDS ([Figure 424(b)(4)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm)); see [[issuers/figure-open|Figure OPEN]].
- **National exchanges** trade tokenized and traditional shares on one order book with equal priority, settled through [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] ([[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]]; [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)).

## Post-trade
DTC's Tokenization Service converts book-entry positions into tokens and back, 2 a.m.-6 p.m. ET on business days, targeting 15 minutes or less. Tokens then move peer-to-peer 24/7 between registered [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)). On-chain netting and digital cash are on the 2027+ roadmap.

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/backeds-xstocks-go-live-today-on-bybit-kraken-and-solana-defi-302494374.html>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>
- <https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq>
- <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm>

# Who can buy
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/who-can-buy


*In plain English: Whether you can buy a given stock token depends on where you live and how the token is structured.*

Who can hold a tokenized stock depends on the structure (see [[overview|the overview]] and [[topics/legal-structures|legal structures]]).

## Offshore wrapped tokens
Most offshore products exclude US persons (xStocks, Ondo, Coinbase, Robinhood) ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary; [Fensory](https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms), secondary). [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] are offered to eligible non-US clients in 110+ countries and are not available in the US, Canada, the UK or Australia ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)).

## US routes
- [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|Broker-dealer]] model: [[issuers/dinari|Dinari]] documents a US broker-dealer route.
- Issuer-sponsored shares can admit eligible US investors, usually behind KYC and a transfer-agent whitelist. Exodus token holders can only trade with holders who passed the [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]]'s AML/KYC and were whitelisted ([Exodus offering circular](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm)). WisdomTree's WTGXX allows transfers only between verified, whitelisted [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] ([WisdomTree FAQ](https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/)).
- Tokenized Securities Venues under the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] are permissioned: access is limited to approved participants ([SEC order 34-106402](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/>
- <https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms>
- <https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf>
- <https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/>
- <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm>

# Coinbase B20
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/b20
type: standard

*In plain English: B20 is the token format Coinbase uses for its tokenized stocks on Base.*

B20 is the Base-native token standard that Coinbase's tokenized stocks use ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks); [Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). It is designed to work for any asset; stocks are one use case.

## Design
- A superset of [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]], built as Rust precompiles and shipped in Base's Beryl upgrade ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)). Standard ERC-20 methods and events work.
- Two variants: **Asset** (6-18 decimals, with a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]]) and **[[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|Stablecoin]]** (6 decimals) ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).
- Built-in controls: transfer policies, freeze-and-reissue, roles, memos, supply caps and permit ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).
- Audited by Base and Spearbit, per the docs ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).

## Tokenized stocks on B20
- **Multiplier**: one token does not always equal one share. Cash dividends are converted to shares and the multiplier rises (e.g. 1.02) ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). Scheduled changes use ERC-8056 `updateUIMultiplier`; the instant `updateMultiplier` is deprecated and kept as a failsafe.
- **Identification**: integrators should identify tokens by contract address, not ticker, and watch the `B20Created` event. A public, keyless API returns addresses, supply, multipliers, ISINs and Chainlink reference values ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- **Access**: secondary transfers are permissionless; [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]] applies to Authorized Participants who [[concepts/glossary#mint|mint]] and [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).

See [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase tokenized stocks]], [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]] and [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]] for a permissioned alternative.

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks>
- <https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20>
- <https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks>

========================================================================
# ERC-1400 / ERC-1410
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/erc-1400
type: standard

*In plain English: ERC-1400 is an older, draft set of Ethereum rules for security tokens that can block or force transfers.*

ERC-1400 (draft, 2018) is an umbrella suite: ERC-1594 (transfer validation, off-chain data), ERC-1643 (documents), ERC-1644 (controller/forced transfers) and ERC-1410 (partitions) ([spec](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md)). ERC-1410 defines balanceOfByPartition, transferByPartition and operator transfers, i.e. "partially fungible" balances useful for lockups and share classes ([ERC-1410](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1410.md)).

ConsenSys UniversalToken is a reference implementation with certificate-based validation ([GitHub](https://github.com/ConsenSys/ERC1400)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md>
- <https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1410.md>
- <https://github.com/ConsenSys/ERC1400>

========================================================================
# ERC-3643 (T-REX)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/erc-3643
type: standard

*In plain English: ERC-3643 is an Ethereum token standard that only lets approved, identity-checked wallets hold or receive the token.*

ERC-3643 is a final EIP. It extends the basic [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]] token with permissions: transfers can be conditional, paused or frozen, forced, or recovered.

A transfer only goes through if two checks pass ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)):
- the **Identity Registry** confirms both parties hold valid ONCHAINID claims, and
- the modular **Compliance** contract approves it.

Compliance modules cover limits such as country, holder count and balances ([ERC-3643 docs](https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/permissioned-tokens)). Reference implementation: [GitHub](https://github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643>
- <https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/permissioned-tokens>
- <https://github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643>

========================================================================
# Solana Token-2022 extensions
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/solana-token-2022
type: standard

*In plain English: Token-2022 is Solana's token program with optional add-ons that tokenized stocks use for compliance and splits.*

Token-2022 adds extensions including transfer hook, permanent delegate, default account state, scaled UI amount and metadata ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions)).
- **Transfer hook**: a custom program runs on every transfer; ExtraAccountMetaList resolves extra accounts. This is Solana's equivalent of identity-gated compliance checks ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook)).
- **Scaled UI amount**: a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] changes the displayed balance without changing raw balances; used for splits and reinvested dividends ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/scaled-ui-amount)).
Used by Ondo Stocks on Solana ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions>
- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook>
- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/scaled-ui-amount>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview>

# BUIDL (adjacent fund precedent)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/buidl-precedent
type: comparison

*In plain English: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, is an early example that later stock-token projects copied.*

BlackRock's BUIDL fund (launched 20 Mar 2024) used Securitize as [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]], tokenization platform and placement agent ([Nasdaq PR](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/blackrock-launches-its-first-tokenized-fund-buidl-on-the-ethereum-network-2024-03-20)). Adjacent to equities: a fund, not a stock. See also [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree]] (funds).

# Implementations compared by model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/implementations-by-model
type: comparison

*In plain English: A side-by-side table of tokenized stock projects, grouped by legal model.*

Classification follows the [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|SEC staff taxonomy]]. Details and sources are on each linked page.

| Implementation | Model | Key mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell\|Superstate Opening Bell]] | Issuer-sponsored | SEC-registered transfer agent; onchain cap table |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize (issuer shares)]] | Issuer-sponsored | Transfer agent book entry |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize Stocks]] | Custodial entitlement | UCC Art. 8 via broker-dealer; Solana PropAMM |
| [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase B20]] | Custodial claim | Beneficial claim; Alpaca custody |
| [[issuers/dinari\|Dinari dShares]] | Broker-dealer mirror record | Tokens mirror off-chain brokerage books |
| [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot\|DTC Tokenized Entitlements]] | Custodial entitlement (post-trade) | DTC participants; NAL |
| [[issuers/ondo-global-markets\|Ondo Stocks]] | Synthetic / note | BVI SPV notes; economic exposure |
| [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood Stock Tokens]] | Synthetic / debt security | Jersey issuer; no rights in underlying |
| [[issuers/bstocks\|bStocks]] | Synthetic / certificate | ADGM certificates over shares |
| [[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]] | Backed tracker | Jersey issuer; multiplier |
| [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv\|OKXICE TSV]] | Venue (TSV) | Permissioned AMM under Innovation Exemption |
| [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model\|Nasdaq / NYSE]] | Venue (exchange) | Same book, DTC settlement |

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

# Coinbase Tokenized Stocks
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks
type: issuer
jurisdiction: Abu Dhabi Global Market (FSRA-authorized, per Coinbase via Zerion)
chain: Base
status: live
last_updated: 2026-10-17

> [!info] At a glance
> **Type:** issuer  
> **Jurisdiction:** Abu Dhabi Global Market (FSRA-authorized, per Coinbase via Zerion)  
> **Chain:** Base  
> **Status:** live  
> **Last updated:** 2026-10-17  

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| name | Coinbase Tokenized Stocks |
| jurisdiction | Abu Dhabi Global Market (FSRA-authorized, per Coinbase via Zerion) |
| product_name | B20 stock tokens |
| structure | Beneficial claim on backing shares |
| chains | Base |
| who_can_buy | Eligible jurisdictions outside the US; offered under Regulation S |
| num_assets | 58 prospectuses listed on coinbase.com/tokenize (2026-10-17) |

*In plain English: Coinbase's stock tokens on Base are each backed by a real share held in custody.*

Each [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]] token on Base is a beneficial claim on a real share in [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]] custody ([Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/tokenize); [Base](https://www.base.org/stocks)). Coinbase holds an FSRA permission in ADGM ([ADGM](https://www.adgm.com/media/announcements/coinbase-establishes-its-tokenization-hub-in-abu-dhabi-with-financial-services-permission-from-the-financial-services-regulatory-authority)).

A public read-only API publishes records, [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multipliers]] and prospectuses ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/overview)).

[[concepts/glossary#authorized-participant|Authorized participants]] (institutional market makers) buy the shares, which go to Alpaca, a regulated broker and [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks); [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/08/24/coinbase-debuts-tokenized-stocks-on-base-network-joining-race-to-bring-equities-on-blockchain), news). Token format: [[standards/b20|B20]].

*In plain English: Figure lets companies issue their shares directly on a blockchain, so the token is the real share.*

Figure's OPEN lets companies issue equity [[concepts/glossary#native-token|natively]] on Provenance, trading via Figure's ATS ([Figure](https://investors.figure.com/news-releases/news-release-details/figure-announces-chain-public-equity-network-open-running)); registration filing announced Nov 2025 ([Figure](https://investors.figure.com/news-releases/news-release-details/figure-announces-public-filing-registration-statement-proposed)).

The Figure announcement page blocked retrieval, so only its headline was checked.

*In plain English: Ondo's stock tokens are notes that track US stocks, backed by shares held at US brokers. They are not the shares themselves.*

The issuer is a [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]] BVI [[concepts/glossary#spv|SPV]]; assets are held at U.S. broker-dealers, overcollateralized, with Ankura as security agent ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)). Tokens are [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]] on [[concepts/glossary#ethereum|Ethereum]] and BNB Chain and [[concepts/glossary#token-2022|Token-2022]] on [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]] ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).

[[concepts/glossary#mint|Mint]] and redeem use signed quotes through IGMTokenManager ([Ondo API](https://docs.ondo.finance/api-reference/overview)).

# Robinhood Stock Tokens
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens
type: issuer
jurisdiction: Jersey

status: live
last_updated: 2026-10-23
